name: Multi-Role Fighter Aircraft (MRFA)
variant: MRFA / Rafale AoN 2026 programme — ~114 multi-role fighter aircraft for the IAF

header.one_liner: The IAF's long-delayed programme to buy ~114 modern multi-role fighter aircraft; a 2026 Acceptance of Necessity (AoN) cleared a large Rafale (and/or follow-on) acquisition to rebuild IAF fighter squadron strength.
header.maker: Programme — Indian Air Force; competing OEMs (Dassault Rafale lead candidate from French ecosystem; others possible)
header.indigenous_label: Imported aircraft with Make-in-India offsets/TOT aspirations

what_it_is.prose: The Multi-Role Fighter Aircraft (MRFA) programme is the Indian Air Force's long-running attempt to acquire a further batch of modern multi-role fighters to rebuild its shrinking squadron strength. After repeated tender launches and postponements, the programme gained fresh momentum in 2026 with an Acceptance of Necessity (AoN) clearing a large acquisition — most prominently reported as a significant Rafale order (the IAF already operates 36 Rafales), although the broader MRFA programme envisages up to ~114 aircraft. The MRFA is intended to complement the indigenous Tejas Mk2 and the future AMCA in the IAF's medium-fighter line-up, and to replace the ageing vintage fleet. A key stated requirement is Make-in-India participation — offsets and increasingly technology-transfer/Rafale-style co-production — so that some aircraft are assembled or partially built in India, though the extent of genuine local content has been a continuing point of contention. The programme is strategically important because it directly addresses the IAF's well-documented shortfall (a 42-squadron sanctioned strength versus an actual count well below that), and it sits alongside the indigenous fighter programmes as the import pillar of India's fighter modernisation. The 2026 AoN marks a decisive step toward actually buying the aircraft, following over a decade of proposals.

deployments_procurement.summary: The MRFA underwent multiple request-for-proposal cycles from ~2018 onward. In 2026 an Acceptance of Necessity cleared a large acquisition (most prominently a substantial Rafale order), giving the programme a concrete procurement path after years of delay. The exact final quantity, value and build/offsets arrangement remain to be finalised in the contract (flagged as uncertain); ~114 is the oft-cited target MRFA ceiling and the 2026 AoN reportedly approves a large first tranche.

faq.question: What is the MRFA programme?
faq.answer: MRFA (Multi-Role Fighter Aircraft) is the IAF's programme to acquire a further batch of ~114 modern multi-role fighters to rebuild its squadron strength, supplementing the indigenous Mk2/AMCA and the earlier 36 Rafales.

faq.question: Why is the MRFA taking so long?
faq.answer: The MRFA has been in and out of re-tender since ~2018 due to repeated disputes over cost, technology transfer, offsets and the terms of Make-in-India participation. The 2026 AoN marks a concrete step toward actually buying the aircraft.

faq.question: Which aircraft is the lead MRFA candidate?
faq.answer: The Dassault Rafale is the lead reported candidate, given the IAF already operates 36 Rafales and the 2026 AoN reportedly clears a substantial Rafale order; however the final type and quantity are to be confirmed in the contract.
